steps.tx: The **PR interval** reflects total conduction time through the atria, **atrioventricular node**, and the His-Purkinje network. Normal values range from **120** to **200** ms. A prolonged interval exceeding 200 ms confirms first-degree block, typically arising within the AV node itself. Shortening under 120 ms suggests accelerated conduction, pre-excitation, or ectopic junctional pacemakers.

steps.tx: A normal **QRS duration** remains strictly under **120** ms. Widening beyond 120 ms signifies substantial intraventricular conduction delay or classic **bundle branch block**. Complete left bundle branch block features broad, notched R waves across lateral leads with secondary ST depressions, causing profound mechanical dyssynchrony. Right bundle branch block displays rsR prime patterns in V1.

left.title: Left Bundle Branch Block
points: QRS duration 120 ms or greater
Broad notched R waves in I, aVL, V5-V6
Absence of septal Q waves in lateral leads
Associated with structural myocardial disease

right.title: Right Bundle Branch Block
points: QRS duration 120 ms or greater
Terminal rsR prime in lead V1
Slurred wide S wave in lateral leads
Frequently seen in pulmonary hypertension

steps.tx: **Left bundle branch block** widens the QRS to 120 ms or more, with broad notched R waves in I, aVL, V5 and V6 and no Q waves in those leads. Newly seen LBBB in a patient with suspected structural disease needs a transthoracic echocardiogram. After TAVR, new LBBB needs continuous telemetry for 48 to 72 hours to detect high-grade AV block. The **Sgarbossa criteria** help detect acute MI in LBBB, and a score of 3 or more confirms it.

steps.tx: The rate-corrected **QTc** calculated by the **Bazett formula** is prolonged when exceeding **450** ms in adult men and **460** ms in adult women. Bazett calculation divides measured QT by the square root of the preceding RR interval. Values surpassing 500 ms confer extreme risk of torsades de pointes and sudden arrhythmic death, mandating immediate electrolyte repletion.

steps.tx: The classic **Sokolow-Lyon index** for **left ventricular hypertrophy** requires the sum of the S wave depth in lead V1 and the R wave amplitude in V5 or V6 to exceed **35** mm. Additional corroborating signs include left atrial enlargement, left axis deviation, and asymmetric lateral ST-segment depression with inverted T waves reflecting left ventricular systolic overload.

rows: S in V1 + R in V5/V6 > 35 mm
R in aVL + S in V3 > 28 mm (M) / 20 mm (F)

steps.tx: The **Cornell voltage** criteria defines left ventricular hypertrophy when the R wave in lead **aVL** plus the S wave in lead V3 exceeds **28** mm in men or **20** mm in women. This criterion demonstrates superior diagnostic sensitivity compared with Sokolow-Lyon, particularly among female patients and obese individuals whose thoracic wall thickness dampens precordial voltages.

left.title: Men Cornell Threshold
points: R wave in aVL + S wave in V3 > 28 mm
Adjusts for larger average male myocardial mass
Correlates with increased cardiovascular mortality
Indicates regression when blood pressure is controlled

right.title: Women Cornell Threshold
points: R wave in aVL + S wave in V3 > 20 mm
Accounts for lower average female chest wall voltage
Identifies subclinical hypertensive target organ damage
Predicts heart failure development with preserved EF

steps.tx: **Wellens syndrome** signals critical stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending coronary artery. Type A demonstrates **biphasic T waves** in leads V2 and V3, while type B demonstrates deep, symmetric inverted T waves. These pathognomonic waveforms typically manifest during pain-free intervals following spontaneous reperfusion. Immediate invasive coronary catheterisation is essential to avert extensive anterior infarction.

left.title: Wellens Type A Pattern
points: Biphasic T waves in precordial leads V2 and V3
Accounts for approximately 25% of cases
Occurs during pain-free post-ischemic state
Normal or minimally elevated cardiac biomarkers

right.title: Wellens Type B Pattern
points: Deep symmetric T wave inversions in V2 to V4
Accounts for approximately 75% of cases
Indicates impending complete LAD thrombosis
Stress testing is strictly contraindicated

steps.tx: The **De Winter pattern** is an acute STEMI equivalent demonstrating upsloping ST-segment depression at the **J-point** in precordial leads with tall, prominent, symmetric T waves. Arising in roughly 2% of acute proximal left anterior descending occlusions, this morphology lacks traditional ST elevation yet signifies complete coronary cutoff requiring emergency percutaneous coronary revascularisation without delay.

steps.tx: The diagnostic **Brugada type 1** electrocardiographic pattern features **coved ST-segment** elevation of **2** mm or greater in right precordial leads followed by a negative T wave. This channelopathy arises from loss-of-function SCN5A mutations. Type 1 findings can be unmasked by fever or sodium channel blockers and indicate high risk for polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.
